Please Note: If you are a current Hydro Ottawa employee with access to Workday, apply to this job via the Workday application. 
 At Hydro Ottawa, we power the lives of the people in the communities we serve.  
 As the electricity distributor to the Nation’s Capital, our work powers the essential activities that make up our lives - at home, at work and at play. And as Ontario’s largest municipally-owned producer of green power, we are leading the way to a greener tomorrow.  
 We are seeking a Grid Technology Specialist who enjoys hands-on work with the support of a collaborative team; a problem solver who always puts safety first. Without you, we’d be in the dark.  
 Are you ready to make a difference in our community? 
 JOB SUMMARY 
 The Grid Technology Specialist is responsible for the administration, design, development, implementation, and maintenance of multiple Class A and Class B Operations Smart Grid Technology Systems. This includes managing distribution asset information and planning the business process integration of GIS and other software based operational systems with other corporate enterprise applications. The Grid Technology Specialist is also responsible for the research, evaluation and recommendation of solutions required for the strategic implementation of all distribution Smart Grid systems for the corporation. 
 MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES 
 The essential responsibilities of the job include but are not limited to the following:
 Responsible for the administration of Class A systems include the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system, the Distribution Management System (DMS), the Outage Management System (OMS), and P-Tech system, as well as Class B systems including the Geographic Information System (GIS) and other systems such as PI , CYME, 4Command, and Computer-Assisted Drafting (CAD).
 Responsible for the design, configuration, provisioning, commissioning, and administration of the Analog, Status and Control points within the SCADA application.
 Responsible for the management, configuration and administration of critical communication components within SCADA, including Channels, Channel Groups, RTUs, Inter-Control Center Communications Protocol (ICCP) connections, and PI connections.
 Responsible for the configuration and administration of alarming in SCADA in accordance with established standards and requirements.
 Responsible for the design, creation and management of all single line diagrams and displays in SCADA.
 Coordinate with IESO, Hydro One, and City of Ottawa Light Rail Transit for ICCP point configuration, commissioning, and maintenance.
 Coordinate  with outside Operations staff including Stations Technicians and Stations Supervisors for integration and commissioning of new field devices.
 Evaluate and test field devices with Distribution Assets, Stations, and Operations groups.
 Responsible for SCADA Incident Response including reporting anomalous or suspicious behaviour, triaging issues and concerns, and take appropriate action as per Hydro Ottawa policies and procedures and escalating to appropriate parties (cybersecurity team, vendor) when necessary.
 First responder to Class A and Class B Grid Technology systems performing triage, investigating, and resolving issues. When required, engaging other groups, coordinating their actions, and ensuring resolutions are reached in a timely manner.
 Researches and evaluates Operations Smart Grid Technology systems software including Class A (SCADA/DMS/OMS/P-Tech), Class B (GIS/PI), other systems (4Command/CYME/CAD), and makes recommendations for their use.
 Administer SCADA (including ICCP) and DMS Oracle databases in the Training and Development System, pre-production, and production environments.
 Configure and maintain OMS and GIS Oracle databases in both development and production environments.
 Administer, configure, and maintain proprietary PI database in the production environment 
 Identify specifications, create fields and tables, and develop/generate reports for databases in Oracle and Access using MS SQL or other platforms for Operations asset records, including distribution circuits, poles, streetlights, manholes, switches, stations, etc.
 Liaise with IT DMI group on the management of Operations electronic databases used by GIS, OMS, SCADA, and other applications.
 Develop criteria and specifications for the proper management of asset data maintained by Operations.
 Design, develop and lead patching of Class A, Class B, and other systems impacting Grid Technology.
 Lead activities for the collection and implementation of Operations field data.
 Automation of system reports and tasks through scripting and software tools.
 Contribute as a member of the Grid Technology team for developing the overall corporate strategy for Operations software applications used in the management of Hydro Ottawa’s distribution grid.
 Develop and maintain documentation for Smart Grid Technology standards and procedures.
 Develop and maintain contacts with suppliers and users, including municipalities and external agencies.
 Assist with the negotiation of Operations Smart Grid Technology supply and support contracts, and to resolve issues as they arise.
 Develop Request for Proposal documents for the provisions of vendor services, evaluates proposals, assists with the negotiation of details, and makes recommendations for implementation.
 Undertake business process administrator responsibility for all Operations Smart Grid technology related software and hardware.
 Provide business process support and liaises with users of Smart Grid Technology solutions and recommends methods of meeting these needs.
 Lead or participate in the development and deployment of business processes and related Operations technologies.
 Provide input to the Grid Technology budget process and generates purchase requisitions.
 Coordinate activities for the conversion of hard copy records to an electronic format.
 Develop and provide training sessions for staff on the use of Operations software applications.
 Develop and deliver oral presentations.
 Ensure that all corporate policies are followed.
 Perform other related duties as assigned.
 EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE 
 A university degree or college diploma in a related technical discipline. 
 Working knowledge of Oracle SQL, Visual Basic / C, Dot Net (.net ) programming languages or equivalent programming languages  including a strong knowledge of Access. 
 Working knowledge of geospatial theories and terminologies.  
 Working knowledge of Microstation and/or AutoCAD digital mapping concepts. 
 Working knowledge of electrical distribution system theory, terminology, and equipment. 
 Strong computer skills; proficient in the use of office productivity and collaboration tools, preferably G Suite. 
 Experience in the development and maintenance of SCADA, GIS or OMS applications considered an asset. 
 Previous exposure to real time software packages such as historical trending packages and ICCP is considered and asset. 
 ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS 
 English Essential, both oral and written 
 Bilingual (French and English) is considered an asset. 
 Valid driver’s license - Class G 
 The terms and conditions of employment for this position are governed by the collective agreement between Hydro Ottawa Limited and IBEW Local 636. 
 Hydro Ottawa offers a Hybrid Work Model. Hybrid work is position specific, the details of which the hybrid model will be discussed with successful candidates. 
 Hydro Ottawa may use artificial intelligence (“AI”) during the recruitment process to aid in the screening and selection of candidates. 
 Location:
Ottawa, ON 
 The terms and conditions of employment for this position are governed by the collective agreement between Hydro Ottawa Limited and the applicable union.
 Pay Range Minimum:
$75,060.70 Pay Range Maximum:
$115,475.10

November 29, 2026 Hydro Ottawa is committed to establishing a qualified workforce that reflects the diverse population it serves and we encourage applications from all qualified individuals. We are also committed to preventing and removing barriers to employment for people with disabilities, and we invite you to inform us should you have any accessibility or accommodation needs.

Position Title:  Peer Support Facilitator – 2SLGBTQI Health & Wellness 
 Employment Status: Temporary Full-Time Contract, until September 29, 2028 
 Position Status: This is a Bargaining Unit position. All terms and conditions of the collective bargaining agreement apply.
 This posting is for an Existing vacancy.
 Job Posting Deadline for Internal Candidates: October 23, 2026, at 5:00pm
 Hours of Work/Schedule: 35 Hours per week (May includes some evening/Night shift)
 Position Reports To: Manager, Integrated Care and Experience  
 Salary Range: Annualized salary range $51,000 - $57,000, commensurate on skills and experience, plus participation in HOOPP.
 Primary Work Location: Pickering, ON (with flexibility to transition or to work at other DCHC sites as required)
 Organization 
 Who We Are: Durham Community Health Centre (DCHC) is a registered charitable organization that provides integrated, accessible, and equitable community-based primary care, wellness services, and health education for Durham community members facing barriers to health and well-being.
 Who We Serve: DCHC offers equity-focused programs and services for priority populations, including Indigenous peoples, Black communities, 2SLGBTQI+ community members, newcomers to Canada, seniors, and clients without a family doctor. This approach helps community members access both preventive care and care when they are ill.
 How We Work: Our interprofessional team includes physicians, nurse practitioners, nurses, counsellors, dietitians, outreach workers, medical secretaries, and administrative staff. Together, we place each client at the centre of care and respond to their needs through integrated clinical care, wellness supports, and health education.
 Why Join Now: This is an exciting time to join DCHC as we advance an energizing path toward greater impact in local health care. Guided by our Strategic Plan, Theory of Change, brand, client stories, and resources, we are diversifying, expanding, and strengthening how we serve the community.
 Position Overview 
 The Peer Support Facilitator will integrate their personal lived experience with gender-diverse healthcare to contribute insight, support, and leadership to services offered by Durham Community Health Centre’s 2SLGBTQI Health & Wellness program.
 Working as a valued member of the Gender Care Team, the Peer Support Facilitator will offer peer-based support, advocacy, and system navigation assistance to clients exploring or affirming their gender identity. This role is pivotal in fostering a welcoming, safe, and inclusive environment where clients feel empowered and supported throughout their journey.
 The Peer Support Facilitator will also bring essential lived experience to inform service delivery, guide program design, and help shape the evolution of DCHC’s future hub-space model for 2SLGBTQI Health & Wellness.
 Key Responsibilities 
 ·          Provide one-on-one peer support to individuals navigating gender identity and gender expression, offering empathetic listening, guidance, mentorship, and emotional support. 
 ·          Facilitate support groups focused on gender-diverse experiences, fostering a safe, inclusive space for sharing and peer connection. 
 ·          Share personal lived experiences, where appropriate, to offer insights and peer-led encouragement. 
 ·          Assist clients in accessing healthcare, mental health, and community services related to gender-affirming care. 
 ·          Advocate for client needs by building bridges between community members and healthcare services, increasing trust and engagement. 
 ·          Contribute lived experience to program design and planning, ensuring services are reflective of client needs and community realities. 
 ·          Represent the 2SLGBTQI Health & Wellness program at community events, outreach activities, and advocacy initiatives. 
 ·          Collaborate with the broader gender care team to promote comprehensive, gender-affirming care and cultural safety. 
 ·          Participate in ongoing training, supervision, and professional development opportunities to strengthen peer support skills. 
 ·          Maintain confidentiality and appropriate professional boundaries at all times.
 Qualifications 
 ·          2-year Diploma in Social Services / Mental Health and Addictions or similar. 
 ·          Strong understanding of the needs, challenges, and barriers facing transgender, non-binary, and gender-diverse individuals in healthcare and social service systems. 
 ·          Demonstrated personal lived experience navigating gender identity and/or gender-affirming care is required. 
 ·          Minimum 2 years of program planning and delivery experience. 
 ·          Peer Support Training Certificate is an asset. 
 ·          Excellent communication, interpersonal, and active listening skills. 
 ·          Ability to work both independently and collaboratively within an interprofessional team environment. 
 ·          Effective organizational, decision-making, and problem-solving skills. 
 ·          Ability to remain flexible, self-reflective, empathetic, and supportive in a dynamic environment. 
 ·          Ability to maintain confidentiality and create a safe space for peer sharing and support. 
 ·          Experience facilitating peer support groups or educational sessions is an asset. 
 ·          Experience working with service users or community organizations is an asset. 
 Key Competencies 
 ·          Strong communicator 
 ·          Collaborative team player 
 ·          Effective interpersonal skills 
 ·          Adaptability to changing priorities and client needs 
 ·          Strong time management and organizational skills 
 ·          Crisis management and problem-solving abilities 
 ·          Empathy and a client-centered approach 
 ·          determine priorities.
 Full vaccination against COVID-19 is mandatory for this position (DCHC will however adhere to its duty to accommodate those who are unable to be fully vaccinated for a reason related to a human right protected ground).
 DCHC encourages applications from individuals who reflect the diversity of the communities served, including Indigenous peoples, racialized persons, persons with disabilities, members of the 2SLGBTQIA+ community, and other equity-deserving groups. 
 Application Process: 
 1.                While we thank all applicants for their interest in applying, only those qualified and considered for an interview will be contacted. All applicant submissions will be kept on file for six months, for future consideration.
 2.                All applicants are encouraged to provide a valid email address for communication purposes. Applicants may receive written correspondence regarding this job posting directly to the email address provided on their resume. As an applicant, it is your responsibility to ensure that you check your email regularly.
 3.                All positions are subject to the successful completion of the following pre-employment conditions for all external hires: Reference Checks; and Criminal Background checks (including Vulnerable Sector Screening).
 4.                Please be advised that AI Technology supports the screening process of applications. All final hiring decisions are made by our recruitment team.
 Durham Community Health Centre (DCHC) is committed to creating an inclusive environment that welcomes and celebrates diversity so that all employees have the opportunity to thrive.  DCHC will comply with all applicable standards as set out in the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, 2005 (AODA), the provisions of the Ontario Human Rights Code, and any other applicable legislation.  Accessibility: If you have accessibility needs and require alternate formats or other accommodation, please contact our Talent and Culture team at 905-723-0036, or by email to recruiting@durhamchc.ca .

The Project Coordinator, Architectural Trades supports the planning, procurement, coordination, installation, inspection, and closeout of architectural construction packages for station and associated building areas. 
 Working closely with the Architectural Project Manager, site supervision, design consultants, quality teams, commercial teams, suppliers, and subcontractors, the Project Coordinator helps ensure that architectural work is executed safely, in the correct sequence, and in accordance with approved drawings, specifications, contract requirements, approved samples, applicable codes, and project quality standards. 
 The position focuses specifically on architectural and building-finish scopes, rather than civil works. These may include masonry, façade, drywall and partitions, ceilings, architectural metalwork, doors and hardware, glazing, roofing, waterproofing, cladding, flooring, tiling, painting, millwork, signage, louvers, firestopping, sealants, and other interior and exterior architectural finishes. 
 The salary range for this position is $90,000 CAD - $120,000 CAD, plus additional benefits.
 Key Responsibilities: 
 Architectural Planning & Coordination 
 Coordinate architectural construction packages from design development and procurement through installation, inspection, deficiency correction, and final turnover.
 Review architectural drawings, reflected ceiling plans, room data sheets, door and hardware schedules, finish schedules, specifications, shop drawings, samples, mock-ups, method statements, and installation details. 
 Confirm that subcontractor shop drawings and technical submittals are coordinated with the latest approved design information before materials are released for fabrication or installation. 
 Identify discrepancies, missing information, constructability concerns, dimensional conflicts, and interface issues affecting architectural work. 
 Prepare, submit, track, and close Requests for Information relating to architectural design, finishes, materials, dimensions, tolerances, interfaces, and installation requirements. 
 Coordinate architectural requirements with structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, communications, security, vertical transportation, and other interfacing disciplines. 
 Work with design and field teams to confirm wall openings, embeds, sleeves, access panels, equipment clearances, ceiling coordination, service penetrations, backing, supports, and finishing requirements. 
 Support the preparation of architectural work plans, look-ahead schedules, installation sequences, access requirements, logistics arrangements, and area-release plans. 
 Coordinate architectural samples, colour selections, material approvals, control samples, first-work inspections, and mock-ups. 
 Maintain architectural trackers for submittals, RFIs, samples, mock-ups, design changes, procurement, installation status, inspections, deficiencies, and closeout documentation. 
 Procurement, Construction, and Field Coordination 
 Assist in defining architectural subcontractor scopes of work and identifying scope gaps, exclusions, overlaps, and trade interfaces. 
 Support the preparation and review of bid packages, technical comparisons, scope clarifications, supplier proposals, subcontractor submissions, and procurement recommendations. 
 Coordinate with procurement teams, suppliers, fabricators, and architectural subcontractors to monitor material approvals, fabrication activities, delivery dates, storage requirements, and installation readiness. 
 Track long-lead architectural materials and equipment, including doors and hardware, glazing systems, cladding, specialty finishes, ceiling systems, architectural metalwork, millwork, signage, and custom-fabricated components. 
 Confirm that materials delivered to site correspond with approved submittals, samples, finishes, colours, quantities, and project requirements. 
 Monitor architectural activities in the field and coordinate with site supervisors and subcontractors to maintain the required work sequence and planned production. 
 Verify that work areas are ready before architectural subcontractors mobilize, including access, preceding-work completion, environmental conditions, dimensions, temporary services, material storage, and protection requirements. 
 Coordinate access, hoisting, work zones, laydown areas, temporary protection, material handling, and interfaces between architectural subcontractors operating in shared areas. 
 Participate in daily coordination meetings, weekly subcontractor meetings, look-ahead planning sessions, design reviews, quality meetings, and progress meetings. 
 Monitor architectural subcontractor manpower, productivity, work fronts, constraints, and scheduled completion dates. 
 Identify and escalate potential delays, incomplete prerequisites, design constraints, procurement risks, coordination conflicts, and quality concerns. 
 Support the development and implementation of practical mitigation and recovery measures. 
 Ensure architectural activities are carried out in compliance with project health and safety requirements, environmental requirements, approved work plans, and site procedures. 
 Quality, Compliance, and Closeout 
 Support quality assurance and quality control activities for architectural work. 
 Verify that architectural installations comply with approved drawings, specifications, shop drawings, samples, mock-ups, manufacturer requirements, inspection and test plans, applicable codes, and project standards. 
 Coordinate inspections with subcontractors, site supervision, quality personnel, consultants, designers, authorities, and other stakeholders, as applicable. 
 Prepare and maintain inspection requests, checklists, deficiency lists, non-conformance records, corrective-action records, and associated quality documentation. 
 Monitor workmanship, alignment, tolerances, finishes, colour consistency, joint treatment, transitions, interfaces, protection, and final appearance. 
 Confirm that concealed architectural work and interfacing conditions are inspected before walls, ceilings, cladding systems, or other finishes are closed. 
 Coordinate testing and specialist inspections related to architectural systems, where required, including water penetration, adhesion, pull testing, sealant, firestopping, door operation, hardware functionality, and other specified performance requirements. 
 Manage architectural deficiencies from initial identification through correction, reinspection, acceptance, and closure. 
 Coordinate room-by-room, area-by-area, or system-based inspections and turnover activities. 
 Support the preparation of as-built drawings, warranties, maintenance information, attic stock records, spare-material inventories, operation and maintenance manuals, training records, product data, certificates, and turnover packages. 
 Confirm that architectural closeout documentation is complete, accurate, properly organized, and submitted in accordance with project requirements. 
 Support final cleaning, protection removal, touch-ups, finish repairs, and the presentation of completed areas for inspection and handover. 
 Progress Reporting, Cost Control, and Change Management 
 Track architectural progress by trade, area, level, work package, or construction zone. 
 Maintain accurate records of completed quantities, planned versus actual progress, outstanding work, constraints, deficiencies, and forecast completion dates. 
 Prepare weekly and monthly architectural progress reports, dashboards, photographs, trackers, and management updates. 
 Assist with schedule reviews and short-term planning for architectural packages, including three-week, six-week, and other project-specific look-ahead schedules. 
 Support quantity tracking, installed-progress measurement, subcontractor progress reviews, and payment-assessment processes. 
 Review subcontractor progress claims against actual work completed, accepted materials, approved changes, deficiencies, and supporting records. 
 Maintain records supporting architectural changes, including instructions, RFIs, site conditions, labour records, material records, photographs, quotations, and schedule impacts. 
 Assist in identifying potential changes, scope growth, rework, design development, and out-of-sequence work. 
 Support the review of subcontractor quotations and change-order documentation for completeness and alignment with the defined architectural scope. 
 Assist with cost forecasting, commitment tracking, accruals, quantity reconciliation, and architectural package cost reporting. 
 Monitor material waste, rework, damage, productivity, and subcontractor performance, and support corrective measures where needed. 
 Maintain accurate daily and weekly records to support progress verification, commercial discussions, schedule analysis, and dispute avoidance. 
 Identify trends, recurring constraints, and opportunities to improve architectural coordination, procurement, installation, inspection, and turnover processes.
College diploma or bachelor's degree (preferred) in Architecture, Architectural Technology, Construction Management, Building Science, Engineering Technology, or another construction-related discipline.
 Two to three years of experience in project coordination, construction coordination, architectural construction, building finishes, or a related construction environment. 
 Experience reviewing architectural drawings, specifications, shop drawings, material submissions, samples, and finish schedules. 
 Experience coordinating subcontractors, suppliers, consultants, and field activities. 
 Experience on large, complex building, transportation, transit, institutional, commercial, industrial, or infrastructure projects involving significant architectural scope is an asset. 
 Experience with interior fit-out, exterior envelope, station finishes, public-facing areas, or high-quality architectural finishes is an asset.
 Ability to read and interpret architectural drawings, reflected ceiling plans, sections, elevations, details, schedules, specifications, contracts, and technical documentation. 
 Understanding of architectural construction methods, materials, finishes, installation sequencing, tolerances, and trade interfaces. 
 Working knowledge of common architectural packages such as masonry, drywall, ceilings, doors and hardware, glazing, waterproofing, roofing, cladding, flooring, tiling, painting, millwork, signage, firestopping, sealants, and architectural metalwork. 
 Ability to compare drawings, shop drawings, specifications, samples, and field conditions to identify inconsistencies and missing information. 
 Strong understanding of the coordination required between architectural installations and mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire-protection, security, communications, and structural systems. 
 Ability to prepare clear RFIs, meeting minutes, deficiency reports, progress reports, technical correspondence, trackers, and supporting change documentation. 
 Strong planning and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple architectural packages, priorities, deadlines, and stakeholders. 
 Strong attention to detail, particularly regarding finishes, dimensions, tolerances, interfaces, approved materials, and documentation status. 
 Effective verbal and written communication skills. 
 Ability to communicate professionally with project managers, superintendents, subcontractors, architects, consultants, suppliers, quality personnel, and client representatives. 
 Ability to work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary project team while maintaining ownership of assigned actions. 
 Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to identify practical solutions to architectural coordination and field-installation issues. 
 Ability to spend time in active construction areas and verify progress and conditions directly in the field. 
 Demonstrated commitment to safety, quality, accountability, teamwork, and continuous improvement. 
 Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, and Teams. 
 Ability to develop and maintain progress trackers, submittal logs, RFI logs, procurement schedules, deficiency lists, quantity records, and reporting tools in Excel. 
 Ability to review, mark up, compare, and organize architectural drawings and technical documents electronically. 
 Experience using construction document-management and collaboration platforms such as Autodesk Construction Cloud, BIM 360, Procore, Aconex, SharePoint, or an equivalent platform is an asset.
 Experience using Bluebeam Revu or similar PDF review and markup software is an asset. 
 Familiarity with AutoCAD, Revit, Navisworks, Primavera P6 or Microsoft Project is an asset.

 Titre du poste: Ingénieur analyste - Systèmes de contrôle
 À propos de Pratt & Whitney Canada 
 Pratt & Whitney Canada (P&WC) est un leader mondial de l’innovation aérospatiale, dont le siège social est situé à Longueuil, au Québec, depuis 1928. Nous concevons et fabriquons des moteurs d’aéronefs de nouvelle génération qui propulsent la plus grande flotte mondiale d’avions et d’hélicoptères dans les segments de l’aviation d’affaires, de l’aviation générale et de l’aviation régionale.
 Depuis près de 100 ans, nos équipes sont à l’avant-garde des technologies de propulsion, repoussant les limites afin de rendre nos moteurs plus performants et fiables. Nos moteurs soutiennent des missions essentielles, du transport de passagers et de marchandises aux services médicaux d’urgence, aux opérations humanitaires et à la lutte contre les feux de forêt, partout dans le monde.
 Un employeur de choix 
 Pratt & Whitney Canada a été reconnue comme l’un des meilleurs employeurs au Canada en 2026 selon Forbes, et ce, pour une 11e année consécutive. L’entreprise s’est également classée au premier rang des employeurs de l’industrie de l’aérospatiale et de la défense au pays. De plus, notre siège social figure toujours parmi les meilleurs employeurs de la région de Montréal. Ensemble, ces distinctions confirment notre réputation d’employeur de choix à Montréal, au Canada et à l’échelle mondiale.
 Pourquoi rejoindre notre équipe? 
 L'ingénieur analyste des systèmes de contrôle sera chargé de concevoir, valider et certifier les systèmes de contrôle des moteurs à turbine à gaz pour les moteurs à turbine à gaz. En tant qu'ingénieur analyste de contrôle, le candidat retenu développera des exigences au niveau des systèmes à-propos des commandes de moteur. Au cours de la phase de conception du moteur / de l'avion, il travaillera avec les fabricants d'avions pour développer la fonctionnalité du système de contrôle. Il travaillera avec une équipe intégrée de produits pour correspondre à la fonctionnalité du système de contrôle par rapport aux exigences des moteurs et des avions. Le candidat retenu devra comprendre la dynamique de la centrale et le processus DO-178B pendant qu’ils préparent les éléments de preuve à l'appui du certificat pour le type de moteur. Il travaillera également en étroite collaboration avec les fournisseurs pour vérifier les logiciels et les données d'examen pour les essais du système de contrôle effectués sur des simulations, le moteur et les avions.
 Le poste s’effectue à notre établissement de Longueuil , du lundi au vendredi, selon des horaires flexibles et exclusivement en présentiel.
 À quoi ressemblera votre quotidien? 
 Créer des exigences du système de contrôle en travaillant en collaboration avec les clients internes et externes.
 Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les département de design de P&WC et d'autres fournisseurs de logiciels pour que le exigences de systèmes sont interprétées et appliquées comme prévu.
 Créer des plans de test du système de contrôle et des procédures utilisées pour valider les systèmes de contrôle sur les simulations des bancs d’essai de simulation et dans un banc d’essai de moteur P&WC.
 Soutenir le département de test de moteurs de P&WC et les bancs d’essai de simulation des fournisseurs afin d'assurer la bonne exécution de l'activité de validation.
 Soutenir les activitées d’essais de vol avec les clients.
 Reviser et interpréter les données d'essai produites au cours des tests de validation.
 Générer des rapports de certification de haut niveau pour ensuite les soumettres aux autorités nationales et étrangères de certification.
 Fournir l'amélioration continue des processus d'organisation, basée sur les leçons apprises grâce à la mise en œuvre.
 Fournir un appui technique au secteur de la fabrication de P&WC pour assurer une transition fluide de nouveaux produits en production.
 Fournir un appui technique au secteur de l'après-vente de P&WC.
 Qu’est-ce qu’il vous faut pour réussir? 
 Diplôme en ingénierie (mécanique, électrique ou aérospatiale).
 5 à 15 ans d'expérience dans l'ingénierie des systèmes de contrôle, en fonction de la position.
 Une compréhension du logiciel de l'aérospatiale DO-178B est nécessaire.
 Ce poste s’inscrit dans un milieu de travail francophone, néanmoins il nécessite une très bonne connaissance de l’anglais pour lire et comprendre, sur une base quotidienne, de la documentation et des termes techniques qui peuvent émaner d’organisations internationales, ainsi que pour écrire et communiquer en anglais avec des clients, des fournisseurs ou des collègues internationaux.
 Qualifications privilégiées 
 Une expérience pertinente systèmes de contrôle des turbines a gaz ainsi que la connaissance du dual channel FADEC seraient considérés atout.
 La connaissance du DO-254 firmware est souhaité.
 Ce que nous offrons 
 Programme de régime de retraite et d’épargne avec cotisation de l’employeur
 Programme d’assurance collective
 Possibilités d’avancement (progression de carrière)
 Programme de mérite ou programme de reconnaissance
 Programme de santé et bien-être, y compris la télémédecine
 Club récréatif et sportif
 Garderies à proximité
 Accessibilité en transport ou programme de transport en commun et stationnement gratuit
 Travailler chez Pratt & Whitney Canada 
 Le masculin est utilisé sans discrimination et uniquement dans le but d’alléger le texte. Nous étudierons la demande d’emploi de tous les candidats qualifiés.
 Chez Pratt & Whitney Canada, nous allions avec passion, audace et rigueur pour concevoir, fabriquer et entretenir les moteurs d’aéronefs les plus avancés et les plus fiables au monde. Notre travail et la qualité de nos produits contribuent au succès de nos clients, qui à leur tour sauvent des vies, soutiennent le commerce, connectent les communautés et protègent les libertés.
 Chez Pratt & Whitney Canada, vous avez l’occasion de faire une différence tous les jours ; il suffit de lever les yeux. Êtes-vous prêt à vous dépasser ?
 Le candidat retenu devra se soumettre à une vérification de ses antécédents judiciaires et obtenir toutes les autorisations nécessaires en lien avec la manipulation et le transfert de marchandises contrôlées.  Job Title: Engineer, Analyst - Control Systems

 Own Asana's security risk management program: Design and continuously mature a quantitative risk framework — including risk scoring methodologies, likelihood and impact modeling, and risk appetite thresholds — that enables consistent, data-driven risk decisions across the organization.

 Better Everyday: make the close, the cash forecast, payments and tax filing a bit faster and cleaner every month, and fix the root cause of every payment or booking error.

DO YOU WANT TO SUPPORT JOBBERINO'S TO DO THEIR BEST WORK?

Then Jobber might be the place for you! We’re looking for a People Business Partner to be part of our People department.

Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. We work with small home service businesses, like your local plumbers, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn’t like it used to be—the way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. That’s why we put the power and flexibility in their hands to run their businesses how, where, and when they want!

Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail’s Canada’s Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada’s Technology Fast 50™, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500™ lists. With an Executive team that has over thirty years of industry experience of leading the way, we’ve come a long way from our first customer in 2011—but we’ve just scratched the surface of what we want to accomplish for our customers https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EkfZmHrRLx4&list=PLoktA_D-2UEnxMLfCe93bANKXVXd2bdN8&index=24.

The team:

The People team builds the environment where Jobberinos do their best work: how people are hired, onboarded, grown, paid, and supported when life gets complicated.

We are a small team, which means a lot of ground to cover and real ownership of it. You are closely embedded in the business and find out quickly when something worked. You’ll work at two altitudes: strategic (the diagnosis and the advice) and execution (the documentation and the follow-through that makes it better next time). AI is how we cover both, and we are rebuilding the way this team works around it rather than running it as a side project.

The role:

Reporting to the Senior Manager, People, the People Business Partner is an intermediate level role embedded in a business unit, and the person leaders go to when they need both practical and strategic support. You adapt frameworks to the situation in front of you, and where there is no precedent, you build the approach. You work independently and check in on the decisions that matter.

This is a hands-on role at both ends of the range. You will partner directly with the senior leaders and executives who run your group, bringing them a recommendation rather than a question. You will spend time coaching managers who are leading people for the first time, becoming their essential partner as they learn, and you will also spend real time on leave administration, performance documentation, and employee relations case management. This role provides a great balance for someone who wants both the strategy and the execution.

You will build for where Jobber is going, not just where it is. Structures will change, manager expectations will shift, and AI will change what a team can do. With your strong business knowledge, you will bring forward your viewpoint to influence the department's health and success.

The People Business Partner will: 

 - Know your group's strategy, structure, and drivers well enough to build a people agenda that gets ahead of capability, engagement, retention, and succession risk.

 - Advise managers and senior leaders across performance, development, compensation, team structure, and change. Communicate for leaders who do not know People, and persuade where you need to.

 - Coach first-time and early-tenure managers through the hard parts of people leadership. Leaving them more capable and equipped to lead afterward.

 - Identify when the same question keeps returning, and build the guidance once to multiply your impact and allow managers to be self-sufficient.

 - Run performance management end to end: expectations, documentation standards, improvement plans, and the difficult conversations and exits that follow.

 - Bring judgment to talent review and compensation cycles: calibration, leveling, promotions, and succession gaps named before someone resigns.

 - Own the employee lifecycle for your group: leaves, accommodations, return to work, internal moves, and exits, including the administration and coordination with managers, payroll, and providers that keeps it accurate and humane.

 - Manage employee relations independently, including ambiguous and legally sensitive cases, with a firm grip on employment legislation and clear escalation when it is warranted.

 - Assess structures, spans of control, and decision rights when performance or growth raises structural questions. Identify a people problem from a design problem, and support leaders through the changes that follow.

 - Track leading indicators across engagement, performance, and retention, run your group's listening cycles, and turn results into action plans leaders commit to.

 - Drive people initiatives end to end. Adapt an existing program where one fits, build the approach where nothing does.

 - Use AI in the work, not around it. Delegate research and drafting to agents so your time goes to judgment, analyze your group's data to arrive at leadership conversations with a point of view, and pressure test your recommendations before you take them forward.

 - Bring forward the gaps. When a manual process or documentation hole keeps generating the same escalation, propose what should replace it.

 - Partner with Talent Development, Total Rewards, and Talent Attraction so your group gets one answer, not three. Stay current on where People practice and tech are heading, and bring what works back to the PBP team, because the pattern you found almost always exists elsewhere.

To be successful, you should have:

 - A proven track record of advising and influencing senior leaders and executives, including the ones who needed persuading and who did not arrive with the problem framed. Ideally somewhere that was growing while you were there.

 - Performance management and employee relations experience you can speak to specifically, including the cases that did not go the way you planned.

 - Experience running performance and compensation cycles end to end for a multi-team group, not supporting someone else's.

Palona’s AI agents operate in real restaurant environments: noisy phone lines, varied accents, complex menus, interruptions, incomplete information, strict business rules, and customers who expect an immediate, natural response. Improving these systems requires more than selecting the newest model. It requires disciplined evaluation, high-quality data, modeling judgment, experimentation, and production feedback loops.
 We are looking for an applied AI Modeling Engineer to improve the intelligence, accuracy, safety, latency, and cost of Palona’s voice and multimodal agents. You will own problems across model selection and routing, prompting and context, fine-tuning or post-training when justified, speech and language quality, evaluation methodology, dataset development, and model behavior in production.
 This is a product-facing modeling role. Research depth matters, but success is measured by improvements that survive contact with production and create better guest, restaurant, and business outcomes. You will work closely with product, full-stack, infrastructure, and customer-facing engineers to move from hypothesis to experiment to reliable deployment.
 What you’ll own
 Develop modeling and experimentation strategies for high-impact agent problems in voice, language, reasoning, ordering, multilingual behavior, and multimodal understanding.
 Build rigorous offline and online evaluations that measure task completion, accuracy, safety, latency, cost, conversational quality, and business outcomes.
 Create and maintain representative datasets from simulations, human annotation, production feedback, and difficult edge cases while protecting sensitive data.
 Evaluate frontier and open-source models and make clear build, buy, route, prompt, fine-tune, or distill decisions.
 Improve prompting, context construction, memory, tool-use policies, structured outputs, model routing, and fallback behavior.
 Design fine-tuning, preference optimization, distillation, or other post-training work when it offers a measurable advantage over simpler methods.
 Partner with speech and real-time engineers to improve ASR, TTS, turn-taking, interruption handling, pronunciation, multilingual behavior, and end-to-end latency.
 Develop analysis tools that explain model failures, slice performance by scenario, detect regressions, and accelerate iteration.
 Ship model changes with production guardrails, staged rollouts, monitoring, rollback paths, and clear quality gates.
 Translate new research and model releases into concrete product opportunities and communicate tradeoffs to technical and non-technical partners.
 Raise scientific and engineering standards through reproducible experiments, thoughtful reviews, and clear documentation.
 3+ years of industrial experience in relevant technical domain.
 Strong machine learning foundations and hands-on experience developing or evaluating production AI systems.
 Strong Python skills and experience with modern ML tooling such as PyTorch, JAX, Hugging Face, or equivalent systems.
 Practical experience with LLMs, speech models, multimodal models, or agentic systems.
 Ability to design reliable experiments, define useful metrics, analyze noisy results, and avoid optimizing against weak proxies.
 Experience building datasets, evaluation harnesses, model services, or training and inference pipelines.
 Strong software engineering judgment; your work is reproducible, tested, observable, and usable by other engineers.
 Ability to connect modeling choices to product constraints including latency, cost, privacy, safety, and user experience.
 Comfort operating in ambiguity and collaborating across research, engineering, product, and customer contexts.
 AI-native working habits and genuine curiosity about new model capabilities and limitations.

The Opportunity
We're looking for a Staff Security Engineer to define and drive Fullscript's defensive threat detection, incident response, and AI-assisted SecOps capability across our cloud infrastructure, identity, endpoints, and application ecosystems.
This role sits at the technical core of our Security function. You will architect modern detection systems, leverage AI/ML to automate SecOps workflows, and establish defensive testing practices for AI threat vectors. Partnering with Engineering and Platform teams, you will ensure our detection and response capabilities scale with Fullscript's fast-growing, AI-first infrastructure.
The ideal candidate has owned enterprise-scale detection engineering and incident response end-to-end. You are a pragmatic, forward-thinking engineer who excels at designing AI-augmented SOC workflows, conducting targeted AI defensive testing, and converting threat telemetry into automated, high-precision detection and response systems.
What You'll Do
Detection Engineering & Defensive Strategy
Set the multi-quarter technical direction for detection and response, and drive it across Security, Platform, and Engineering teams.
Architect, author, and maintain advanced detection logic across SIEM, cloud infrastructure, identity systems, endpoint protection, and AI/ML pipelines.
Establish detection coverage and defensive controls against emerging AI and agentic threat vectors (e.g., prompt injection, tool misuse, and data exfiltration patterns).
Own the full rule lifecycle, from authoring and testing through tuning and retirement, and measure it against concrete signals: detection coverage, precision (false-positive rate), and time-to-detect.
Create and maintain dashboards and reporting that give leadership visibility into alert volume, response times, and trends over time.
AI-Augmented Security Operations & Automation
Design and deploy AI-assisted investigation workflows that leverage LLMs and automated agents to accelerate triage, context enrichment, and threat containment.
Build and extend internal security tooling to support identity resolution, cross-source log correlation, and natural-language querying over security telemetry.
Automate the handoff between detection tooling and our ticketing system so investigations move from alert to resolution with minimal manual work.
Incident Response & Investigations
Lead and support security investigations end-to-end, from initial triage through containment and resolution.
Mentor Security Operations team members and set the standards the team builds against, including rule quality, detection-as-code practices, and investigation rigor.
Partner with relevant teams across the business to investigate and remediate security escalations surfaced from Customer Support, Customer Delivery, and internal teams.
Maintain and improve response playbooks based on lessons learned from real investigations.
Participate in an on-call rotation to respond to security incidents outside business hours.
AI Defensive Testing & Validation
Threat model new and existing systems, including AI agents and services, to identify what could go wrong, what we would need to see to catch it, and how we would respond.
Lead defensive testing, purple-teaming, and adversarial validation exercises to test alert fidelity and evaluate detection resilience against AI-driven threats.
Partner with Platform and Engineering teams to ensure new AI services and features expose necessary logging and telemetry for effective security monitoring.
Evaluate authorization and access-control changes for security-relevant blast radius, and drive remediation with the engineering teams that own the affected systems.
Threat Intelligence
Operationalize threat intelligence into actionable detections and tracked follow-up work.
Coordinate indicator of compromise (IOC) blocking across endpoint, network, and web layers.
What You Bring to the Table
8+ years of experience in detection engineering, incident response, or security engineering, with demonstrated leadership in shaping organizational security strategy.
Practical experience incorporating AI tooling into SecOps workflows, along with familiarity with detection strategies for AI-specific threat vectors.
Strong scripting/automation skills (Python, JavaScript, or similar) and experience building workflows in a SOAR-style or workflow automation platform.
Experience managing security controls as code (e.g., Terraform), with changes made through peer review rather than manual console changes.
Experience securing cloud environments (AWS preferred) and modern SaaS/identity stacks.
Hands-on incident response experience: triage, investigation, containment, and postmortem/playbook development.
Working knowledge of adversary tradecraft (MITRE ATT&CK) and the ability to translate it into practical, tuned detections rather than noisy alerts.
Proven ability to partner directly with engineering and infrastructure teams to define telemetry and control requirements for systems you don't own.
Excellent written communication. This role regularly turns investigation findings into clear, factual updates for technical and non-technical stakeholders alike.
Bonus if You Have
Experience contributing to or building from open detection content, such as Sigma rules or community rule repos.
Experience collaborating with red/purple-team exercises to validate detection coverage.
Experience supporting a healthcare, regulated, or otherwise highly sensitive-data environment.
Relevant certifications (GCIH, GCFA, GCTI, GCDA, or equivalent practical experience).

   Job Summary 
 Responsible for assisting design, development, implementing and maintaining of enterprise-wide customer premises equipment (CPE) activation, provisioning, and operations applications and their associated operating systems and databases. Responsible for Application Administration of CPE activation, provisioning, and operations platforms applications supporting all Atlantic Broadband.  Job Responsibilities 
 ●       Installs, administers, configures and maintains CPE activation, provisioning, and operations applications including operating systems and related software
